You are an independent fact auditor for a driver-permit study course. You did not write these facts.
For EACH fact, check its statement ONLY against the text of the handbook page it cites (pages are given by physical PDF page number). Never use outside knowledge, memory, or other states.
Verdicts: SUPPORTED = the cited page states it (paraphrase is fine if the meaning, numbers, conditions and exceptions all match). PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED = mostly right but a number, condition, exception or scope differs or is missing. NOT_FOUND_ON_PAGE = the cited page does not state it. CONTRADICTED = the cited page says something incompatible.
evidence_quote: a verbatim quote of at most 25 words from the cited page that decides the verdict ("" if nothing relevant is on the page). issue: one sentence ("" when SUPPORTED). suggested_fix: a corrected statement grounded only in the page ("" when SUPPORTED).
Return exactly one finding per fact, in the same order, and a summary whose counts equal the findings. Output JSON only.

{"state":"Hawaii","handbook":"Hawaii Driver's Manual 2023","section_id":"sec13-backing-lanes-speed-turns-passing-brakes","facts":[{"fact_id":"sec13-F01","statement":"Hawaii law forbids a driver or any adult passenger from leaving a child under nine years old unattended in a motor vehicle for five minutes or longer, because of dangers such as extreme heat, theft of the car, or accidental use of the emergency brake, power windows or trunk release.","pdf_page":64,"printed_page":"6644"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F02","statement":"Backing is dangerous because visibility is restricted, so check the area behind the vehicle before getting in, turn around and look to the rear instead of relying on mirrors whose view is too small, and have someone outside guide you if you cannot see.","pdf_page":64,"printed_page":"6644"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F03","statement":"When backing, apply the brakes gently as the movement starts to confirm they work, always back slowly, watch the front of the vehicle for clearance when backing and turning at once, and avoid backing into or across a roadway, parking so that you can enter traffic forward.","pdf_page":64,"printed_page":"6644"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F04","statement":"When traffic is clear, back only into the lane nearest the edge of the roadway, and the chief responsibility for avoiding a collision rests with the driver leaving a parking space, who should look, signal and yield.","pdf_page":64,"printed_page":"6644"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F05","statement":"Use extraordinary caution when backing in residential areas, because children often play behind and between parked vehicles.","pdf_page":64,"printed_page":"6644"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F06","statement":"Entering from a driveway you must always stop before crossing the sidewalk area, since failing to stop is unlawful, then move forward slowly watching for pedestrians and vehicles, make sure the lane is clear, enter the nearest lane with a right turn when possible, and accelerate to traffic speed.","pdf_page":64,"printed_page":"6644"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F07","statement":"From a parallel parking space you move forward into the nearest lane when there is enough gap in traffic, while leaving a diagonal space requires backing into the lane first, a much more dangerous and difficult maneuver that takes more time.","pdf_page":65,"printed_page":"6655"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F08","statement":"A roundabout is a one-way circular intersection serving drivers, pedestrians, pedestrians with disabilities and bicyclists, in which entering traffic must yield to circulating traffic, and each approach carries a yield sign and may have yield line markings.","pdf_page":65,"printed_page":"6655"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F09","statement":"Driving a roundabout, slow on approach, yield to pedestrians and bicyclists when entering and exiting, look left and yield to traffic already circulating including bicyclists, drive to the right of the central island counterclockwise at low speed, signal right to exit, and if you miss your exit go around again.","pdf_page":65,"printed_page":"6655"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F10","statement":"With one lane in your direction you must use it, taking great care in congested areas, and with two lanes in open free-flowing traffic you use the right lane and the left lane only for passing or when vehicles are entering from the right, while in heavy traffic you may use either lane but keep up with traffic at a steady speed without lane hopping.","pdf_page":65,"printed_page":"6655"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F11","statement":"With three or more lanes in your direction, choose the center lanes where there are fewer conflicts, leave the right and left lanes for vehicles entering and leaving, keep a steady speed with the flow with few lane changes, and use the right lane if you are slower than other traffic.","pdf_page":65,"printed_page":"6655"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F12","statement":"Lane changes should be kept to a minimum, and before one you check conditions ahead, to the sides and behind using the mirrors and a physical head-turn check of the blind spots, then signal well in advance, the law requiring a signal for at least one hundred feet before the change begins.","pdf_page":65,"printed_page":"6655"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F13","statement":"With ample clearance, move gradually and steadily into the other lane, because abrupt movements can cause overcontrol or loss of control, and it is better to slow slightly and move in behind a vehicle, keeping it in sight, than to speed up and cut in ahead.","pdf_page":66,"printed_page":"6666"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F14","statement":"Never force your way into a gap at or below the minimum safe following distance, because that discourteous move makes other drivers close ranks against you, whereas allowing time and signaling properly leads courteous drivers to make room.","pdf_page":66,"printed_page":"6666"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F15","statement":"Always yield to vehicles in the other lane when changing lanes, join a congested lane at the end of the line rather than crowding in ahead, stay in your lane until the change can be made safely even if inconvenient, and never change lanes while approaching or moving through an intersection or crosswalk.","pdf_page":66,"printed_page":"6666"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F16","statement":"Excessive speed for conditions is the most often listed cause of crashes, its underlying cause, whether intoxication, inattention or competition, is controlled directly by the driver, and most vehicles can reach speeds far beyond what the driver, the road and the vehicle can handle.","pdf_page":66,"printed_page":"6666"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F17","statement":"A safe vehicle speed is adjusted to traffic, weather and road conditions and always stays within the posted limits.","pdf_page":66,"printed_page":"6666"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F18","statement":"Keep pace with traffic, because vehicles moving the same direction at the same speed never collide while moving faster than traffic creates constant conflicts, and if you cannot keep up, move as far right as possible.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F19","statement":"Striking the vehicle ahead is one of the most common crashes and usually comes from following too closely, so check your interval by noting when the vehicle ahead passes a tree, pole or other marker and counting one thousand one, one thousand two, and if you reach the word two before you reach the marker you have at least the two-second interval you should never go below.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F20","statement":"Following too closely cuts your view of road and traffic conditions ahead, constantly changing speed confuses other drivers and bursts of speed with heavy braking are wasteful and dangerous, so maintain a steady speed.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F21","statement":"Reduce speed in poor road or weather conditions for better control and more time to react, and never let emotions set your speed, because being in a hurry may mean never arriving at all.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F22","statement":"Turns are changes of direction from a lane at intersections or driveways while curves are changes in the direction of the road itself, and for a turn you get into the proper lane well in advance, turn from the lane nearest the turn direction into the nearest available lane, and if you are in the wrong lane continue on and turn elsewhere rather than forcing a last-minute lane change.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F23","statement":"Make precise turns without swinging wide or cutting short, slow to a proper speed before a curve or turn and hold a steady speed through it, because braking or an abrupt speed change in a turn or curve can cause loss of control.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F24","statement":"Avoid left turns and U-turns whenever possible because they conflict more with traffic, are much more hazardous than right turns and impede other vehicles.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F25","statement":"When waiting to turn left at a red light and the light turns green, move slowly into the intersection with the wheels pointed straight ahead and turn only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F26","statement":"Watch with great care for pedestrians, bicyclists and motorcyclists when turning, since vehicles, darkness or weather may hide them, always come to a complete stop before a right turn on a red signal, use extra caution on curves and turns in poor weather or on gravel, sand or mud, and do not drive in a bike lane when turning right at an intersection.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F27","statement":"Passing is hazardous on two or three lane roads because the opposing lane must be used and improper procedure can cause a head-on collision, so pass only when the vehicle ahead is moving below the safe speed, never merely because it is there or to gain a few car lengths in moderate or heavy traffic, and in a line of vehicles let those ahead pass the leader first.","pdf_page":68,"printed_page":"6688"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F28","statement":"Pass on the left except when the vehicle being overtaken is making or about to make a left turn, in which case pass carefully on the right but never by driving onto the shoulder, and obey every sign and marking that restricts passing.","pdf_page":68,"printed_page":"6688"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F29","statement":"To pass, keep enough following distance to see opposing traffic, check ahead for conflicting traffic, signal left, physically check behind for anyone passing you, sound the horn so the driver ahead knows, accelerate to passing speed in your own lane, then move left and pass.","pdf_page":68,"printed_page":"6688"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F30","statement":"If a conflict appears before the pass is complete, brake sharply and drop back behind the overtaken vehicle instead of speeding up, because speed can be cut more quickly with the brakes than it can be gained with power, and return to your lane only when the overtaken vehicle is visible in your interior rear-view mirror.","pdf_page":68,"printed_page":"6688"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F31","statement":"Where two or more lanes run in your direction, never use an opposing lane to pass; pass on either side with proper lane change procedure, being extra careful on the right because you approach in the other driver's blind spot, and in every passing situation never pass while approaching or moving through an intersection or crosswalk.","pdf_page":68,"printed_page":"6688"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F32","statement":"Parked cars block your view of vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians and may pull out or open a door into your path, so watch for movement in or near the vehicle, lit stop, back-up or signal lamps, exhaust smoke or vapor, and turning front wheels, and assume a driver who has just parked will open the door.","pdf_page":69,"printed_page":"6699"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F33","statement":"Stopping unnecessarily in a traffic lane is dangerous, discourteous, inconsiderate and illegal, so stops to load or unload or to talk with others must be made in a parking space, loading zone or other place out of the lane.","pdf_page":69,"printed_page":"6699"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F34","statement":"Do not stop within an intersection or crosswalk, and never drive into an intersection or crosswalk unless there is room for your entire vehicle on the far side.","pdf_page":69,"printed_page":"6699"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F35","statement":"Brakes stop a vehicle by turning its energy of motion into wasted heat, so every braking wastes fuel money and wears brakes and tires, and careful braking without bursts of speed followed by hard stops saves energy and money.","pdf_page":69,"printed_page":"6699"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F36","statement":"A hard brake application can make wheels slide, and sliding wheels, especially the front ones, leave you without control of the vehicle.","pdf_page":69,"printed_page":"6699"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F37","statement":"When in danger of hitting a vehicle, person or object, do not jam on the brakes and slide the wheels, because you will almost certainly hit it; instead apply and release the brakes rapidly and steer toward a clear area, even off the road, while avoiding people, trees, utility poles and solid structures, and consult the owner's manual for antilock brakes.","pdf_page":70,"printed_page":"70"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F38","statement":"Avoid braking while turning by slowing beforehand, brake very cautiously on water, ice, snow, frost, sand or gravel, and after driving through water test the brakes and, if they are weakened, apply them lightly several times until normal action returns.","pdf_page":70,"printed_page":"70"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F39","statement":"Resting your foot on the brake pedal lights the stop lamps and misleads following drivers and also partly applies the brakes in many vehicles, causing excessive wear, and a brake warning lamp that lights when you brake means a partial failure needing immediate repair.","pdf_page":70,"printed_page":"70"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F40","statement":"Begin slowing as soon as braking ahead becomes apparent, brake smoothly and steadily, and when stopping in traffic stay far enough back to see where the rear tires of the vehicle ahead meet the road, which leaves room to go around if it cannot move.","pdf_page":70,"printed_page":"70"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F41","statement":"Prolonged braking heats the brakes and makes them much less effective, which can usually be avoided by shifting to a lower gear so the engine helps hold the speed down.","pdf_page":70,"printed_page":"70"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F42","statement":"Downshifting means selecting a lower gear range while moving, works with manual and automatic transmissions, and serves two purposes, greater engine braking when slowing or holding speed on a downgrade and better performance when accelerating.","pdf_page":70,"printed_page":"70"},{"fact_id":"sec13-F43","statement":"Downshift for engine braking before starting down a steep grade because shifting is harder at higher speeds, and on a synchronized manual transmission the procedure is to depress the clutch, move the lever to the next lower gear and release the clutch slowly, while double clutching on a non-synchronized transmission should not be tried without practice.","pdf_page":70,"printed_page":"70"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R01","statement":"When a conflict appears mid-pass you brake and fall back, while speeding up to finish the pass is the move the manual forbids.","pdf_page":68,"printed_page":"6688"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R02","statement":"To check for a safe following gap of at least two seconds, watch the vehicle ahead pass a roadside marker and count one thousand one, one thousand two before reaching that spot.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R03","statement":"In a roundabout you look left and yield to circulating traffic, while to leave it you signal with the right turn signal.","pdf_page":65,"printed_page":"6655"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R04","statement":"Changing lanes requires yielding to the vehicles already in the other lane, while changing lanes at or through an intersection or crosswalk is never allowed at all.","pdf_page":66,"printed_page":"6666"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R05","statement":"With two lanes in open traffic the right lane is the travel lane and the left is for passing, while with three or more lanes the center lanes are the travel lanes and the outer lanes serve entering and leaving traffic.","pdf_page":65,"printed_page":"6655"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R06","statement":"A vehicle turning left may be passed carefully on the right, while passing on the shoulder is prohibited in that same situation.","pdf_page":68,"printed_page":"6688"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R07","statement":"In an emergency without antilock brakes you pump the brakes and steer clear, while jamming the brakes slides the wheels and removes steering control.","pdf_page":70,"printed_page":"70"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R08","statement":"While waiting to turn left on green you keep the wheels straight and creep into the intersection, while a right turn on red always begins with a complete stop.","pdf_page":67,"printed_page":"67"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R09","statement":"Leaving a driveway requires a stop before the sidewalk, while backing out of a parking space places the chief collision responsibility on the driver leaving the space.","pdf_page":64,"printed_page":"6644"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R10","statement":"Leaving a parallel space is a forward move into the nearest lane, while leaving a diagonal space means backing into the lane, which is slower and more dangerous.","pdf_page":65,"printed_page":"6655"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R11","statement":"Downshifting before a steep grade lets the engine hold speed, while prolonged braking on the grade overheats the brakes and weakens them.","pdf_page":70,"printed_page":"70"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R12","statement":"A child under nine may not be left alone in a vehicle for five minutes or more, while children playing behind parked cars are the reason for extra caution when backing in residential areas.","pdf_page":64,"printed_page":"6644"},{"fact_id":"sec13-R13","statement":"A driver who has just parked should be WARNING!  Do not leave children unattended.
Hawaii law prohibits you or any adult passenger from leaving a child, under nine years
of age, unattended in a motor vehicle for five minutes or longer. Leaving a child unsu-
pervised in a vehicle can have tragic consequences, such as the child suffering from
extreme heat exposure or injury when the car is stolen or when parts of the car, such
as the emergency brakes, power windows, and trunk releases, are used inadvertently.
BACKING YOUR VEHICLE
Backing is a dangerous maneuver because of restricted visibility and should be
done with great caution. Y ou should use the following procedures to back a vehicle
with safety:
• Visually check the area to the rear of the vehicle before entering.
• Turn around and look to the rear; do not rely on rear-view mirrors. The view
through rear-view mirrors is too small to use for this purpose.
• If you cannot see to the rear, have someone outside of the vehicle guide you.
• When the backing movement is first started, apply the brakes gently to insure
proper operation
• Always back at a slow rate of speed.
• Watch the front of the vehicle for clearance if you are backing and turning at
the same time.
• Avoid backing into traffic. Try to park the vehicle so that you will enter traffic
in a forward direction. Always back into the lane nearest the edge of the road-
way when traffic is clear.
• Avoid backing across or into a roadway whenever possible.
LOOK BACK BEFORE 
DRIVING FROM CURB
LOOK. SIGNAL. YIELD
The chief responsibility for avoiding a collision lies with the driver who is leaving
a parking space. 
Exercise extraordinary caution when backing up in residential areas. Children
often play behind and between parked vehicles.
ENTERING TRAFFIC
Entry into traffic is usually made from a driveway or a roadside parking position.
Y ou should use the following procedures to enter traffic safely:
Entry fr om a Driveway
• Always stop before entering the roadway. The stop should be made before
crossing the sidewalk area. Failure to stop is unlawful.
• Move forward slowly. Watch for pedestrians and oncoming vehicles.
• Insure that the traffic lane is clear of oncoming vehicles.
• Enter the nearest lane in a right turn whenever possible.
• After you are in the traffic lane, accelerate to traffic speed.

Entry fr om a Roadside parked P osition
• If parallel parked, move forward into the nearest traffic lane when there is suf-
ficient space in oncoming traffic.
• If diagonal parked, you will have to first back into the traffic lane. This is a much
more dangerous and difficult maneuver and requires more time to complete.
ROUNDABOUT
A roundabout is designed to meet the needs of all roadway users---drivers,
pedestrians, pedestrians with disabilities, and bicyclists. A roundabout is a one-way
circular intersection in which entering traffic must yield the right-of-way to circulat-
ing traffic. Each road approaching the roundabout is marked with a yield sign and
may also have yield line markings on the pavement. 
Tips for driving through a roundabout:
• Slow down as you approach the roundabout.
• Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists as you enter and
exit the roundabout.
• Look to the left for traffic and yield to traffic, 
including bicyclists, already in the roundabout.
• Drive to the right of the central island and proceed
in a counterclockwise direction.
• Keep your speed low while in the roundabout.
• Use your right turn signal to exit the roundabout.
• If you miss your exit, drive through the roundabout again until you reach your 
exit.
CHOOSING A PROPER TRAFFIC LANE
One Lane in the Direction of Travel.Y ou have no choice; you must use that lane.
In congested areas you must use great care to avoid conflicts with other vehicles and
pedestrians.
Two Lanes in the Direction of Travel.In open area when traffic is free-flowing, use
the right lane; use the left lane for passing or when vehicles are entering from the
right. In heavy traffic or in congested areas use either lane but keep up with traffic.
Move at a steady speed. Avoid continual lane changing (lane hopping).
Three or More Lanes in the Direction of Travel.Choose the center lanes as there
will be fewer traffic conflicts. Leave the right and left lanes available for vehicles enter-
ing and leaving the roadway. Maintain a steady speed with the flow of traffic and keep
lane changes to a minimum. Use the right lane if you are moving slower than other
traffic.
LANE CHANGING
Lane changes should be kept to a minimum as it is a movement that could conflict
with other traffic.
When a lane change is necessary, use the following procedures:
• Check highway and traffic conditions ahead, to the sides, and to the rear. Use
your rear-view mirrors and physically check the blind spots (turn your head and look).
• Signal your intention well in advance. The law requires that you signal for at
least 100 feet (30m) before you start the lane change.

ment into the other lane. A VOID ABRUPT MOVEMENTS: YOU MA Y
OVERCONTROL OR LOSE CONTROL OF YOUR VEHICLE. It may be
necessary to adjust the speed of your vehicle slightly to avoid conflict with traf-
fic. It is best to slow slightly and move in behind a vehicle than it is to speed
up and cut in ahead. When you move in behind a vehicle, you always have that
vehicle in sight and there is less annoyance to its driver.
• Don’t force your way into the space between vehicles that have the minimum
safe following distance or less. This is a discourteous and dangerous action
which causes other drivers to reduce the spacing interval between vehicles to
deny you space to change lanes. If you allow ample time and signal properly,
other courteous drivers will be inclined to allow you space to make the change.
• ALW A YS YIELD TO VEHICLES IN THE OTHER LANE WHEN CHANG-
ING LANES. If the desired lane is congested, enter at the end of the line; don’t
run up ahead and crowd in. If you cannot make the lane change at the desired
location, remain in your lane until you can safely make the change; even if you
are inconvenienced.
• NEVER CHANGE LANES WHEN APPROACHING OR MOVING
THROUGH INTERSECTIONS AND CROSSW ALKS.
VEHICLE SPEED
“Excessive speed for conditions” is most often listed as the cause of crashes. The 
cause of the excessive speed is seldom determined but whether it is due to intoxication,  
inattention, competition, etc., it is directly controlled by the driver. Un  fortunately, 
most vehicles can attain speeds that are far beyond the capabilities of the driver, the 
road, and the vehicle itself.
The proper safe vehicle speed must be adjusted to traffic, weather, and road con-
ditions and should always be within the posted speed limits.
66
Y ou should use the following procedures in maintaining a safe vehicle speed:
• Keep pace with traffic. V ehicles moving in the same direction at the same speed 
never collide. If you move faster than other  traffic, you constantly cause addi-
tional conflicts with other vehicles. If you cannot keep up with traffic, move as 
far to the right as possible.
• Maintain a safe following interval. One of the most common types of crashes, 
striking the vehicle ahead, is usually caused by following too closely. T o insure 
adequate interval, note when the vehicle ahead is opposite a tree, a telephone  
pole or other marker, then start counting at a normal rate “one thousand one, 
one thousand two, etc. ” If you get to the word two before your vehicle reaches 
the marker, you have at least a two second interval. Y ou should never have less. 
Following too closely reduces your ability to see road and traffic conditions 
ahead and you will be unable to avoid trouble when it develops.
• Maintain a steady speed. Constantly changing speed confuses other drivers as 
to your inten tions. Bursts of speed and heavy braking are both wasteful and 
dangerous.
• Reduce your speed when you encounter poor road o r weather conditions. At 
slower speeds you can maintain better control of your vehicle and you will have 
more time to avoid dangerous situations.
• Never let your emotions determine the speed of your vehicle. Never be in a 
hurry, you may never arrive at all.
TURNS AND CURVES
Turns are changes of direction from a traffic lane made at intersections or drive-
ways. Curves are changes in direction of the road or traffic lane. In some cases,  the
safe procedures are similar:
• Get into the proper lane for a turn well in advance. Turn from the traffic lane
nearest the direction of the turn and into the nearest traffic lane available. If you
are not in the proper lane when you want to turn, continue on and make the turn
elsewhere. Don’t force your way into the proper lane or make abrupt last
minute lane changes.
• Make precise turns; don’t swing wide or cut short.
• Slow to a proper speed before you enter a curve or begin a turn. Maintain a
steady speed while in the curve or turn. Braking or an abrupt change of speed
in a turn or curve can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.
• Avoid left and “U” turns whenever possible. These turns conflict more with
other traffic, are much more hazardous than right turns and also impede other
traffic.
• Use great care in watching for pedestrians, bicyclists and motorcyclists when
making turns; they may be hidden by other vehicles, darkness or poor weather.

“Excessive speed for conditions” is most often listed as the cause of crashes. The 
cause of the excessive speed is seldom determined but whether it is due to intoxication,  
inattention, competition, etc., it is directly controlled by the driver. Un  fortunately, 
most vehicles can attain speeds that are far beyond the capabilities of the driver, the 
road, and the vehicle itself.

Y ou should use the following procedures in maintaining a safe vehicle speed:

far to the right as possible.

striking the vehicle ahead, is usually caused by following too closely. T o insure 
adequate interval, note when the vehicle ahead is opposite a tree, a telephone  
pole or other marker, then start counting at a normal rate “one thousand one, 
one thousand two, etc. ” If you get to the word two before your vehicle reaches 
the marker, you have at least a two second interval. Y ou should never have less.

OVERTAKING AND PASSING
Overtaking and passing another vehicle is hazardous on two or three lane roads
where a lane for traffic moving in the opposite direction must be used to complete the
passing maneuver. Improper procedures can cause a head-on collision. Use the fol-
lowing procedures for safe passing:
• Pass only if the vehicle ahead is moving below the safe speed.
• Don’t attempt to pass a vehicle ahead simply because it is there.
• Don’t attempt to pass vehicles merely to gain a few car lengths in moderate or
heavy traffic.
• In a line of vehicles, allow the vehicles ahead to pass the lead vehicle before
you attempt to pass.
• Pass on the left except when the vehicle you are overtaking is making or about
to make a left turn. Pass vehicles making left turns carefully on the right.
NEVER DRIVE ONTO THE ROAD SHOULDER TO PASS A VEHICLE
MAKING A LEFT TURN.
• Obey all signs and traffic lane markings which restrict or prohibit passing.
• Allow ample following distance between your vehicle and the overtaken vehi-
cle so that you can observe any opposing or conflicting traffic.
• Check ahead to see that there is no opposing or conflicting traffic, then SIG-
NAL that you intend to move to the left.
• Physically check behind to see that there are no vehicles attempting to pass
your vehicle.
• Sound your horn so that the driver ahead knows that you are going to pass.
• Accelerate to passing speed in your lane of travel. Then move left and begin to
pass.
• If a conflict appears before you have completed passing, brake sharply and
return to the lane behind the overtaken vehicle. Do not attempt to increase your
speed to complete passing. Speed can be reduced more quickly by applying the
brakes than it can be increased by applying more power.
• Move back into the proper traffic lane when you can see the overtaken vehicle
in your interior rear-view mirror.
On roadways where there are two or more lanes for traffic moving in the same
direction, do not move into a lane for opposing traffic when attempting to pass. Y ou
may pass a vehicle on either side by using the proper lane change procedures. Be extra
careful about passing on the right because you will approach the overtaken vehicle in
the driver’s blind spot.

INTERSECTION OR CROSSW ALK.

PASSING PARKED CARS
Use care when passing cars parked by the roadside. These vehicles obstruct your
view of possible conflict with other vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians. Be alert to the
possibility that a parked car may suddenly move into your traffic lane or that a door
may be opened into the path of your vehicle.
Watch for these clues:
• Movement within the vehicle or within the vicinity of the vehicle.
• Stop lamps, back-up lamps or signal lamps that are illuminated.
• Smoke or visible vapor from the exhaust pipe.
• A turning movement of the front wheels.
When you approach a vehicle that has just stopped in a parked p osition, assume
that the driver will open the door as you approach.

requires that the engine speed for the lower gear range be matched with the vehicle

don’t just jam on the brakes and slide the wheels; you will almost certainly strike the

If the brake warning lamp on the instrument panel lights up when you apply the

Always start slowing your vehicle as soon as it becomes apparent that brakin g

“Downshifting” is the procedure of selecting a lower transmission gear range 
while the vehicle is in motion. This procedure can be used with both manual and auto-
matic transmissions. Downshifting is used for two purposes: (1) T o obtain greater 
braking action from the engine when reducing speed or when maintaining a reduced 
speed on a downgrade; and (2) to obtain increased performance when accelerating to 
a higher speed.
